risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Auditors drew attention to accumulated losses that may cast significant doubt on the Company's ability to continue as a going concern; financial statements are prepared on a going concern basis considering management's plans and continued financial support from promoters.
- A petition relating to ownership of equity shares of the Company is pending before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) under Section 59 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- The subsidiary was wound up with a consequent write-off of investment and loan receivable in the previous financial year.
- Interest income on the loan given to MIJL has not been accrued due to uncertainty of realization; recoverability of investment and loan balances is assessed on an impairment basis.
- The Company has not maintained proper records showing full particulars, including quantitative details and situation of fixed assets, and no physical verification of fixed assets has been conducted by management during the year or in the recent past.
- Auditor noted that reasonable steps for recovery of overdue loans exceeding 90 days have not been taken.
- Lower realization in both export and domestic markets, disturbed power supply, and skilled labour shortage in the region have affected industry and company performance; production is not expected to reach pre-pandemic levels within the next five years.
- Cautionary statement flags global and domestic demand-supply conditions, finished goods prices, raw material costs and availability, exchange-rate fluctuations, and changes in government regulations and tax structure as factors that could materially affect operations.
